01WHY THIS MATTERS

Wearable IMUs - the accelerometers and gyroscopes inside smartphones and dedicated sensors - offer a continuous, low-cost channel for inferring movement and posture. Converting that raw signal into a usable activity indicator is the foundational step behind fall detection, rehabilitation monitoring, and continuous movement sensing.

This project compares two strategies for that conversion on a real benchmark, directly informing how a raw-signal-to-indicator pipeline should be built.

02DATASET

UCI HAR: 30 subjects performed 6 activities (walking, walking upstairs, walking downstairs, sitting, standing, lying) wearing a waist-mounted smartphone. Signal was sampled at 50 Hz and segmented into 2.56s windows (128 readings) with 50% overlap, across 9 raw channels - body acceleration, body gyroscope, and total acceleration, each on x/y/z.

10,299 windows split by subject into 7,352 train / 2,947 test, so no individual appears in both sets.

03TWO PIPELINES COMPARED

04METHODS
  • Feature engineering - per channel: mean, std, min, max, RMS, zero-crossing rate, spectral energy, dominant FFT frequency (8 stats × 9 channels = 72 features/window).
  • Random Forest - 200 independently-grown trees, majority vote.
  • SVM - RBF kernel, C=10, max-margin boundary in non-linear feature space.
  • XGBoost - 300 boosted trees, each correcting the previous trees’ errors.
  • LSTM - 1 layer × 64 units + dropout + softmax(6), trained 20 epochs directly on raw windows, no feature design.

06KEY FINDINGS
1pt
XGBoost vs. LSTM gap is essentially a tie - 91.25% vs 90.16% - despite the LSTM using zero hand-designed features.
64×
Compute cost, not accuracy, separates them - the LSTM took 182s to train vs. 2.86s for XGBoost.
100%
LAYING is solved by every model - its gravity signature is unambiguous regardless of approach.
SIT/STD
Static-posture confusion persists everywhere - the hardest pair for all four models, classical or learned.
Fig. 3 - Per-class F1. The SVM’s deficit is concentrated almost entirely in the three walking classes - an unscaled-feature artifact, not a general weakness.
Fig. 4 - LSTM accuracy climbs to ~90% by epoch 15 and plateaus; the small train/val gap shows dropout controlling overfitting.
07IMPLICATIONS FOR DEPLOYMENT

A pipeline built entirely on raw signal is practically viable: the LSTM recovered, with no domain knowledge, predictive information on par with 72 deliberately engineered features. Equally, hand-crafted features paired with a boosted tree remain a strong, cheap, interpretable baseline. The right choice is a deployment question - inference latency, retraining cadence, need for explainability - not an accuracy question, since accuracy was nearly tied.

08NEXT STEPS
  • Standardize features and re-test SVM to isolate the scaling artifact.
  • Benchmark per-window inference latency, not just training time.
  • Try a 1D-CNN front end feeding the LSTM to close the residual gap.
  • Subject-independent k-fold validation for variance estimates.
Data: Reyes-Ortiz et al., Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones, UCI Machine Learning Repository PORTFOLIO PROJECT
